package_info.package_versions: various (dozens of malicious modules, specific versions not listed)
package_info.why_malicious: The IconBurst campaign distributed dozens of npm packages containing obfuscated JavaScript code designed to steal form data from applications and websites that included them. The packages were typosquats of popular modules, targeting downstream users for credential and data theft.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when included in a web application and executed in the browser)
execution_context.file_location: index.js or main JavaScript file of the malicious npm package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into HTML form submissions, collects form data, and sends it to a hardcoded external domain via HTTPS POST, enabling credential and sensitive data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting form submissions and exfiltrating data to an external domain is a classic data theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages should not silently intercept user input and send it to third-party servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form analytics or telemetry libraries may collect anonymized usage data, but with user consent and transparency.

attack_chain.action: Malicious npm packages are published with names similar to popular packages (typosquatting).
Malicious package is included in downstream applications and websites.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed in user browsers.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript hooks into form submissions and exfiltrates data to attacker-controlled domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data (credentials, PII, etc.).

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that hooks or overrides HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit
Network requests to unknown or suspicious domains during form submission
Obfuscated or minified code with references to fetch/XHR and external endpoints
file_indicators: npm packages with names similar to popular modules but with minor typos
Presence of obfuscated JavaScript in package main files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the application
Domains used in known supply chain attacks (e.g., malicious-domain.com/collect)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with suspicious or typosquatted names. Analyze package contents for obfuscated code and hooks into form submission events. Use runtime monitoring to detect unexpected outbound network requests from web applications, especially during form submissions. Flag any code that exfiltrates form data to untrusted domains.
